📰 Position News — July 27, 2026

⚠️ CAPR — Capricor Therapeutics — WATCH (not urgent, but time-sensitive)

FDA Briefing Documents — OVERDUE AND UNCONFIRMED: Per Federal Register (docket FDA-2026-N-6771), documents were due ≥2 business days before Jul 29 = Fri Jul 25. As of today Jul 27, no media outlet (Fierce Biotech, BioPharma Dive, STAT News) has reported their release across 11+ searches. This is a mildly positive signal — when briefing docs flag major efficacy concerns, biotech press typically blasts them within hours of posting. The absence of negative coverage is reassuring but NOT a confirmation of a clean review. Action: Check fda.gov/advisory-committees → CTGTAC Jul 29 meeting directly. Do this tonight or Monday morning.

Clinical position unchanged: HOPE-3 Phase 3 met all endpoints — primary PUL v2.0 (p=0.029, 54% slowing of decline) and cardiac LVEF (p=0.041, 91% slowing of decline) plus all Type I error-controlled secondaries. FDA lifted its own prior CRL after reviewing HOPE-3 data. Cash runway $279M through Q4 2027. No competing drug in the cardiac DMD indication (Dyne Therapeutics targets skeletal exon skipping — different indication). Stock posted first weekly gain in 5 weeks in the week of Jul 21–27.

Why stock is depressed vs analyst targets ($49–55 avg, $63 high): (1) AdCom adds uncertainty vs straight PDUFA path, (2) Russell index removal forced institutional selling early July, (3) Standard binary event de-risking. The ~33% decline from peak is technical/positioning, not data deterioration. Story is intact.

No material negative news found. Competition (Dyne/Sarepta) is in different DMD mechanisms. No CRLs issued to competing programs in cardiac DMD.

📚 Today you learned

Expected Value (EV) Thinking for Binary Events

EV is the probability-weighted average return across all possible outcomes — the math behind whether a binary trade is rational to take. For your CAPR position: EV = (0.60 × +$233.40) + (0.40 × −$118.60) = $140.04 − $47.44 = +$92.60 positive expected value. That's why the trade made sense at entry — not a guarantee of winning this specific event, but correct over many similar setups with these parameters. The critical discipline: don't move your exit target mid-event. Your GTC at $33–35 locks in the EV calculation you agreed to at entry. Chasing to $45 on a positive reaction introduces new, unplanned risk. Calculate EV before entering. Honour it during the event. That's where the edge lives — not in real-time adjustments.

Also today: Kelly Criterion — optimal position size = (P × b − q) / b. For CAPR at 60% probability with 1.97:1 win/loss ratio: Kelly fraction ≈ 40%. Your 41% position is almost exactly Kelly-optimal — the sizing was correct.
